sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Nepenthes rajah is a carnivorous plant of Borneo, endemic to Mount Kinabalu and Mount Tambuyukon in Sabah. It grows on wet, loose soils at about 1,500–2,650 m; its stem can reach nearly 3 m.

sections.title: Leaves and pitchers
sections.text: The leaves are about 20–50 × 9–13 cm. The large terrestrial pitchers are usually 20–35 cm high and 11–18 cm wide, sometimes reaching 40 cm; their broad, ribbed peristome rims the trap opening.

sections.title: Flowers and conservation
sections.text: Male and female flowers are borne on separate plants. The pitchers trap mainly invertebrates; small mammals may also be found in them. Kew classifies the species as Endangered and it is listed in CITES Appendix I.
